LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` safety gate executes only the top-level scope of the PKGBUILD when it is sourced, and does not invoke any functions. In this PKGBUILD, every top-level statement is either a comment, a plain variable assignment (pkgbase, pkgname, epoch, pkgver, pkgdesc, url, arch, license, makedepends, source, sha512sums, _lgdir), or a shell function definition such as `prepare()`, `build()`, and the various `package_*()` functions. Bash only parses function bodies when they are defined; it does not execute them. Since none of these functions are called during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the loops, `cd`, `patch`, `cmake`, and `make` commands inside them never run. The `source` array entries are merely stored as strings and no download, unpacking, or eval occurs at top level. There is no top-level code execution, network request, or dangerous command in this PKGBUILD that could run during this narrow gate. The suspicious-looking build logic is confined to function bodies that are out of scope for this step.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Only safe assignments and function definitions exist at top level.</summary>
</security_assessment>
